local_articles.title: Manchester City signs global partnership with Trendyol
local_articles.snippet: Manchester City has announced that Trendyol is set to become the club’s official online marketplace partner. Trendyol, one of the world’s leading e-commerce platforms, was founded in Istanbul in 2010 and now connects more than 40 million customers with over 250,000 sellers across a growing international footprint. A committed supporter of football in its home market of Türkiye, Trendyol is an official sponsor of the Turkish National Football Teams and the title sponsor of the Turkish Süper Lig and the First League. It was also an official partner of UEFA Euro 2024. Through this partnership, Trendyol will work with the club to create bespoke content and campaigns, in addition to having a presence across the Club’s digital and social platforms, and branding at the Etihad Stadium. questions.title: Who will be exercising the duties of governor of Mexico's Sinaloa state on August 21, 2026?
questions.background: Sinaloa's governor took a leave of absence on May 1 after being indicted by U.S. prosecutors on drug-trafficking charges. The question concerns who actually performs the governor's duties, rather than who retains the title while on leave.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Mexican government statements and contemporaneous news reporting identifying the person exercising Sinaloa's gubernatorial duties on August 21, 2026. Resolution Rule : If the elected governor remains on leave, resolve to the acting governor. If the elected governor has resumed duties by that date, resolve to the elected governor. Accepted Answer Format : The officeholder's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Rubén Rocha Moya's April 29, 2026 U.S. drug-trafficking indictment and May 1 leave of absence, Sinaloa's Congress swore in former Secretary of Government Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde as interim governor on May 2 and confirmed in early June that Rocha's leave is indefinite pending the FGR probe; she remained in office as of June 18. Given slow U.S.-Mexico evidence exchanges and the severe political cost to President Sheinbaum and Morena of returning a U.S.-indicted governor during Trump administration pressure, Bonilla Valverde is favored (~65%) to remain exercising gubernatorial duties on August 21 (either as interim or substitute governor). However, because Sheinbaum and Mexico's FGR publicly dismissed the U.S. indictment as lacking conclusive evidence, there is a meaningful ~25% chance the FGR clears Rocha Moya and he resumes duties before August 21, plus a small chance Sinaloa Congress selects another senior Morena figure as substitute governor.

questions.title: Which armed group will the United States explicitly identify as an Iranian proxy in an August 2026 designation update?
questions.background: The United States uses counterterrorism designations and financial sanctions to target armed organizations and their funding networks.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official U.S. Treasury or State Department announcement issued during August 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous reliable reporting. Qualifying Event : The announcement must explicitly update an armed group's existing U.S. designation to identify that group as an Iranian proxy. A statement alleging Iranian support without announcing a designation update does not qualify. Resolution Date : The date the qualifying designation update is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the armed group whose designation is updated.
questions.current_reasoning: The June 2026 US-Iran MOU did not address Iran's regional proxies, creating strong pressure on Treasury and State to use updated terrorism designations in August 2026 to maintain leverage. Updating an existing FTO/SDGT designation to explicitly identify a group as an Iranian proxy points to groups already designated where proxy status is either being newly codified or reinforced—such as the Houthis (redesignated FTO March 2025), Hamas, Al-Shabaab (amid US intelligence on Iran/Houthi weapons transfers), Kata'ib Hezbollah, or Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Because dozens of designated groups could receive an OFAC/State designation update, probabilities are kept calibrated (sum 0.47).

questions.title: As of August 20, 2026, which tournament will Carlos Alcaraz have confirmed as his planned return from his wrist injury?
questions.background: Carlos Alcaraz withdrew from the Barcelona Open in April 2026 because of a wrist injury, leaving the timing of his return to competitive tennis uncertain.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from Carlos Alcaraz, as reported by reliable sports-news outlets. Resolution : Identify the tournament named in his most recent public confirmation available by August 20, 2026, as his intended first tournament back following his April wrist injury. Resolve according to his confirmed comeback plan, not whether he subsequently participates. Accepted Answer Format : The tournament's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-08 Alcaraz injury timeline update (Reuters/Straits Times/Al Jazeera Aug 4-5, AS USA Aug 6, La Verdad/Tennis365/Yahoo Sports Aug 6-7, Global Tennis News Aug 8): (1) Carlos Alcaraz officially WITHDREW from the August 13-23 Cincinnati Open on Aug 4 due to his ongoing right-wrist injury without ever having made a formal public confirmation of playing Cincinnati — collapsing Cincinnati Open from 0.62 -> 0.00. (2) Critically, AS USA (Aug 6) clarifies the withdrawal does NOT reflect a medical setback: Alcaraz returned to full-intensity outdoor training this past week (including a public hitting session in Alicante on Aug 3) and simply needed 1-2 extra weeks before competitive play. (3) As of Aug 8 (Global Tennis News), Alcaraz has still made no public confirmation statement, leaving two dominant candidates ahead of the Aug 20 resolution cutoff: (a) US Open (Aug 30-Sept 13, defending champion, currently the ONLY ATP tournament entry list he remains on) rises 0.28 -> 0.53 as the clear primary target, since top-3 stars rarely play an ATP 250 the week before a major (Alcaraz hasn't played a 250 since Feb 2024) and typically arrive early in New York for practice sets instead; (b) Winston-Salem Open (ATP 250, Aug 23-29, main draw wildcards announced around Aug 14-20) enters #2 at 0.27 after Murcian insider daily La Verdad and AS USA reported Alcaraz already holds an invitation and his camp is seriously weighing a wildcard to test his wrist in 1-3 best-of-three matches after 4.5 months without competition. (4) If a late training flare-up forces him to pull out of New York before Aug 20, AS USA notes his remaining post-US Open commitments/schedule are Laver Cup (Sept 25-27, already officially on Team Europe roster -> 0.05), Japan Open in Tokyo (replacing China Open on his fall schedule -> 0.03), and Shanghai Masters (0.02). Top-5 sum = 0.90, leaving 0.10 outside for Davis Cup, China Open, Six Kings Slam, or no explicit public confirmation by Aug 20.

local_articles.title: Reports about poor conditions on USS Abraham Lincoln are ‘completely misrepresented’, says Pete Hegseth
local_articles.snippet: PANAMA CITY - US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Aug 13 that reports about poor conditions aboard aircraft carrier the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East were “completely misrepresented.” Two military-focused outlets, Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, reported suicide attempts and declining morale on the 5,000-person ship, which has been at sea since November 2025. The carrier has been in the Middle East since January, supporting the US war with Iran. “We make sure every ship, every crew, every captain has everything we can provide them at every single moment. Some deployments are longer than others, and I have more respect and gratitude for those sailors than anybody. What they do in those high seas in those austere conditions with less port calls – it’s incredible,” Hegseth told reporters during a visit to Panama. local_articles.title: Senators demand inquiry into conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
local_articles.snippet: WASHINGTON - Congressional Democrats demanded answers on Aug 12 about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, following reports of food shortages, broken plumbing and mental health crises during the aircraft carrier’s record-setting deployment. In a letter to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Aug 12, Senator Richard Blumenthal called for the Navy to account for conditions aboard the aircraft carrier, which “has been deployed more than 250 days” without coming ashore “in over 200 days, setting a record for consecutive days at sea.” Blumenthal voiced concern for such extended deployments, noting “widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns” and other problems aboard the Lincoln.
